WINDOWS ADDS TIGHTER CONTROLS FOR AI AGENTS
articles.summary: Microsoft announced new Windows controls for AI agents, including preview improvements to process containers and experimental hardware-isolated micro VMs. Generally available learning modes let IT observe agent behavior before enforcing restrictions, while Intune is previewing automatic updates for applications employees install themselves.

articles.title: OPTIMIZELY BREACH SPREADS MALWARE ACROSS MAJOR WEBSITES
articles.summary: Attackers exploited Optimizely's experimentation software to distribute malicious JavaScript through websites belonging to at least 178 organizations. The payloads targeted cryptocurrency wallets and payment details. Optimizely says it patched the vulnerability, removed injected code, and revoked tokens.

articles.title: WHEN AI-GENERATED DATA BECOMES TOMORROW'S GROUND TRUTH
articles.summary: Enterprise AI-generated conclusions can lose their original context and become treated as established facts when integrated into operational systems, allowing errors to spread across dashboards, reports, and training data. Decision lineage addresses this problem by linking AI-generated assertions to their source evidence, governing workflows, and downstream decisions. This allows organizations to trace changes, identify affected systems, and systematically correct outdated or inaccurate conclusions.

articles.title: MICROSOFT AND SALESFORCE INTRODUCE COPILOTFORCE
articles.summary: Microsoft and Salesforce announced integrations connecting Salesforce with Copilot, Teams, and Fabric. A Copilot plugin is available in public preview with more than 38 sales skills, letting employees retrieve customer information and take supported actions under their existing Salesforce permissions.

articles.title: TEAMS GAINS MORE PROTECTION AGAINST IMPERSONATION
articles.summary: Microsoft is introducing new capabilities to combat social engineering and impersonation across Teams meetings and calls. These updates include Impersonation Protection to warn users about suspicious participants, an automated skill for the Facilitator agent to scan transcripts for deceptive requests, and a Microsoft Defender data table for forensic investigations.

articles.title: OPEN DATA SHARING: SHARE LIVE DATA BEYOND SNOWFLAKE
articles.summary: Snowflake has launched Open Data Sharing, enabling data providers to share Apache Iceberg tables with external consumers using Iceberg REST Catalog-compatible clients without requiring a Snowflake account or scheduled data exports. This new feature complements existing Snowflake pathways by extending data distribution capabilities to mixed technology environments.

articles.title: GOOGLE, AMAZON AND MICROSOFT: THREE API ESTATES, AND WHAT A SOURCE OF TRUTH DOES
articles.summary: An analysis of Amazon, Google, and Microsoft's API catalogs shows that consistency depends on maintaining a single machine-readable source of truth rather than relying on organizational practices alone. While vendor specifications provide a reliable baseline for API operations, all three companies lack sufficient agent readiness capabilities, particularly around workflows, costs, and lifecycle management.

articles.title: AN OPEN-SOURCE E-READER PROJECT CONFRONTS THE AI CONTRIBUTION FLOOD
articles.summary: Crosspoint Reader has passed 300,000 installations, bringing open-source firmware to tiny, inexpensive e-readers. Its growth also illustrates the pressure AI-generated contributions put on volunteer maintainers, who must review submissions and manage feature requests within tight hardware limits.
